baseline: 18424801. The Word paginator and desktop page index are unchanged by the intervening editorial, Deck and Sheet changes.
scope: A changed body PAGE, SECTIONPAGES or NUMPAGES in reused pages queues its verified section. A section changing size or exit number enqueues any affected fields in other sections, including earlier totals. Physical location follows the original section/block identity. Reuse the last verified window first on undo. A single budget of 16 pages / 256 blocks is shared across the edit, alternative boundaries and repeated field visits. Unsupported boundaries use the existing complete paginator. Native viewport page offsets are rebuilt with the changed scene.
regression: The old incremental path could only reuse a distant field section with identical page count and exit. The new compositor initially still used the old page height index; after the edit, Go To the last physical page never installed its raster on either native desktop. Updating that index fixed both native runs. All twelve PDF fields were checked against the exact physical leaf and numbering restart. The existing six-page paint probe still repaints only the edited page and reuses its neighbour.
fallback: Rebuild the baseline Word pagination and GUI sources together to restore full layout for remote changes in field-section size. Native and CLI saves use standard DOCX; both generations independently rewrote and reopened the final files. Retain full pagination when any boundary, page or block budget fails.
coverage: The layout regression covers plain, odd-page and even-page starts, a display-number restart, asymmetrical mirrored margins, and continued footnotes. Each of the five configurations compares insertion, undo and redo against cold full pagination, every page scene, hit and line index. The prior over-budget case still exercises a complete fallback. Each release program performs 20 alternating insertions and deletions per run and compares all page scenes/hits on the first two edits, plus affected and neighbouring pixels and PDF bytes.

additionalTestLint.note: The extra test-target lint still reports existing test coding-style findings. The product lint and first-party library lint are recorded separately.
